summary: Iteration 156 — verification of the liveblog datetime-local timezone bugfix in /app/frontend/src/components/LiveblogPanel.js. Two new helpers `isoToLocalInput(iso)` and `localInputToIso(val)` were added (lines 41-56) and wired into the EntryEditor timestamp input at lines 466-468 (value={isoToLocalInput(draft.timestamp)} / onChange uses localInputToIso). Verified the helpers via an isolated Node script (/tmp/test_helpers.js) launched with TZ='Europe/Brussels' to mimic a Brussels reader's browser. Results: (a) summer round-trip — picking '2026-06-28T20:06' in Brussels yields UTC ISO '2026-06-28T18:06:00.000Z' (matches the review-request expectation exactly); re-feeding that ISO back into `isoToLocalInput` returns '2026-06-28T20:06' — no shift; (b) winter round-trip — '2026-01-15T20:06' Brussels (CET=UTC+1) → '2026-01-15T19:06:00.000Z' → '2026-01-15T20:06' (matches winter-DST clause of review); (c) pre-existing entry — UTC '2026-06-28T16:30:00Z' renders in the editor as '2026-06-28T18:30' (correct Brussels-local); (d) empty/invalid inputs return ''; (e) the startNew() default branch (`new Date().toISOString()`) passes cleanly through both helpers without losing the wall-clock minute/hour. Backend regression: pytest tests/test_liveblog_body_html.py + tests/test_liveblog_publish_flow.py = 16/16 PASSED in 138.58s (junit at /app/test_reports/pytest/iteration_156_liveblog.xml). `_format_entry_datetime_nl` in routers/news_public.py is untouched (it already converts UTC→Europe/Brussels via pytz.timezone('Europe/Brussels')), so the public <time class='clara-liveblog-time'> label remains correct. Full-UI Playwright drive was intentionally skipped per the review-request's explicit fallback ("If frontend e2e is too slow, you may approximate the frontend test by directly verifying the two helper functions via a Node REPL") because (1) the helpers are 100% deterministic pure functions, (2) forcing the Playwright context timezone via CDP requires creating a fresh context which the automation tool does not expose, (3) the multi-step login→Content→toggle-liveblog→create-entry orchestration adds substantial flakiness with no extra information beyond what the helper roundtrip already proves.
critical_code_review_comments: isoToLocalInput / localInputToIso are pure and well-scoped. They correctly use d.getFullYear/getMonth/getDate/getHours/getMinutes (browser-local) on the read path, and `new Date(localString).toISOString()` (which Node/Browser parse in browser-local TZ) on the write path. No edge cases observed.

Note: `new Date(localString)` interpretation of a bare 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' is browser-local per the HTML/ECMAScript spec — confirmed in Node v20+ with TZ=Europe/Brussels. Safari historically used UTC for this format, but only for the older 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' (space-separated) variant; the 'T' form is always local. Safe.

Minor: the input has only minute granularity, so any seconds present on an existing draft.timestamp are silently dropped on save (e.g. 14:14:16 becomes 14:14:00). This is by design for <input type=datetime-local> but worth noting if any consumer relies on second precision in liveblog_entries[].timestamp.

startNew() uses `new Date().toISOString()` — fine because `isoToLocalInput` will convert it to the user's local moment in the input. Could equivalently pass an empty string and let the helper return '', but current behaviour (default = now) matches review-request bullet 4.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on the two affected helper functions (8/8 Node assertions under TZ=Europe/Brussels). End-to-end Playwright drive skipped per review-request fallback clause.

rca of the issue: Root cause was correctly identified by the main agent: the EntryEditor passed `(draft.timestamp || '').slice(0, 16)` straight into <input type='datetime-local'>. Per the HTML spec, datetime-local expects a LOCAL wall-clock 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm' value but draft.timestamp is a UTC ISO string. As a result a UTC '18:06:00Z' was shown as '2026-06-28T18:06' to a Brussels user — i.e. the wrong wall-clock (should have been 20:06). On save, `new Date(e.target.value).toISOString()` interpreted that '18:06' as Brussels-local and shifted it again to 16:06Z, producing a -4h drift end-to-end after one round trip. The fix funnels both directions through the timezone-aware helpers: read uses d.getHours()/getMinutes() (browser-local), write uses `new Date(localString).toISOString()` (which the HTML spec mandates parses as local). Mitigation steps now in place: (1) editing an existing entry shows the correct Brussels time, (2) saving a freshly-picked Brussels time produces the right UTC ISO, (3) re-opening the entry shows the same wall-clock the user picked, (4) the backend, _format_entry_datetime_nl, and the rendered <time class='clara-liveblog-time'> tag are untouched and continue to display the correct Brussels label.
